title: Generating Routes & Controllers
description: Detailed guide on route and controller generation

sections.title: The -r flag
sections.content: The -r (makeRoute) command generates both a route definition file and its corresponding controller. It automatically maps standard REST endpoints to controller methods, creating a complete communication layer for your resource in one step. See the [CLI Mapping Table](../tables/cli-mapping.md) for a full list of flags.

examples.explanation: Generate a full route and controller for the 'user' resource.
Generate a full route and controller for the 'user' resource.

sections.title: The -c flag
sections.content: The -c (makeCtrl) command is used when you only need to generate the controller logic without the route file. This is useful for adding logic to existing routes or creating specialized controllers that don't follow the standard REST pattern. See the [CLI Mapping Table](../tables/cli-mapping.md) for a full list of flags.

examples.explanation: Generate only the controller for the 'user' resource.
Generate only the controller for the 'user' resource.

sections.title: Filtering CRUD Methods
sections.content: Both -r and -c commands support method filtering via --only and --except flags. You can specify a comma-separated list of CRUD methods (create, readOne, readAll, update, delete) to include or exclude from the generated controller. See the [CRUD Method Mapping](../tables/cli-mapping.md) for details on each method.
